reader.decision_reason: Sunday has the lowest write traffic (~40/s vs ~95/s on Saturday), needs no plan change, and still finishes four days before the 12 November deadline. The thin-slack risk is stated, but nothing in the message shows step 1 is likely to slip.

reconstruction.problem: Step 3 of the PostgreSQL 14 to 16 upgrade of thornbury-ledger has no date. It is the pg_upgrade --link run on pg-thornbury-1, and it must finish before PostgreSQL 14 reaches end of life on 12 November. Step 1 is the pg_partman 5.1 upgrade on 14, booked for Wed 4 Nov. Step 2 is a gate of two nightly pg_partman runs, which complete by Fri 6 Nov 03:30 UTC.
reconstruction.what_breaks: If step 1 slips or a nightly run fails, the Sunday 8 Nov slot is lost. The next slots are Mon 9 to Wed 11 Nov at about 130 writes/s. Sunday 15 Nov is after the deadline. Choosing Saturday 7 Nov instead means about 95 writes/s during the ~14 min downtime.
reconstruction.fix: Book step 3 for Sunday 8 Nov 2026, 02:00 UTC, and change docs/upgrade-plan.md to say 'Step 3 is booked for Sunday 8 November 2026, 02:00 UTC.' The alternative is Saturday 7 Nov 02:00 UTC, which keeps Sunday as a low-traffic retry slot.
reconstruction.cost: Sunday leaves thin slack: a failed prerequisite pushes the run to a weekday slot at higher traffic. Saturday costs higher write traffic (~95/s vs ~40/s) during about 14 min 10 s of downtime. Downtime is the same on either day.
